title: Phase 0: the debts that get more expensive every PR
delivered: i18n retrofit: every string in app/ now resolves through the catalog — t() was previously imported by nothing while ~2,400 lines of UI hardcoded English
§15.3 lint gate: JSX text and person-readable attributes must come from the string layer, in app/**/*.tsx and src/ui/**/*.tsx
Catalog gate: keys used in code must exist in the default locale, and a translated catalog must neither miss keys nor carry orphans
Client components take strings as props — catalogs stay server-side, and the locale is resolved once per request by app/i18n.ts
THEME_LABELS and BUSINESS_TYPES labels moved out of src/ into the catalog: English in src/ is text the gate cannot see
Country, currency and timezone option lists now built server-side in the instance's locale, not client-side with a hardcoded 'en'
Merge completeness gate: schema reflection fails the build when a contact_id column has no entry in CONTACT_REFERENCES
contacts.merge repoints from a declared list the handler actually iterates, so the list cannot drift from the code
Rate limiting declared on the service definition, so it applies to the admin UI, REST API, server actions and MCP alike
The limiter commits outside the caller's transaction — a failed login rolls back, and a counter that rolls back with it counts nothing
auth.login throttled per email address; a successful sign-in clears the budget; 429 carries Retry-After
Security headers on every response: nosniff, DENY, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS
pnpm audit --audit-level high in CI, with four advisories cleared by pinning transitive deps forward rather than lowering the bar
updated_at maintained by the column ($onUpdate) instead of by every write path remembering
contacts.resolve now enriches a known contact (§4.6): blanks fill, owner-entered values never overwrite, first-touch source is kept, lifecycle only moves forward
truncateSpine derived from the tables barrel, closing a hand-list that was drifting
ROADMAP.md: the phased plan from here to the spec'd vision
MASTER.md §7 records the freeholder.ai-before-money-path deviation that had been governing the work from a session note
HANDOFF.md deleted per its own instructions; the local-development facts it carried moved into CONTRIBUTING.md
French and Spanish catalogs, complete and gate-verified, with provenance recorded in locales/README.md as AI-drafted and awaiting native review
openFollowUps: fr and es are AI-drafted and have had no native review — locales/README.md says so plainly, and correcting a phrase is a no-issue-needed first PR
auth.registerOwner is throttled by one global bucket, not per IP: nothing populates `ip` on that path, and threading a trusted client address through Server Actions needs a proxy-trust decision
rate_limit_counters has no sweep — rows are bounded by distinct subjects attempted, but it wants a job once core/jobs exists
The i18n gate covers JSX text and a named attribute list; a user-facing string built in a plain .ts helper and passed to JSX would still pass
Locale is the business default only; the URL prefix (§4.9) and Contact.preferred_locale arrive with the public surface, and both change app/i18n.ts alone
Error messages thrown by services are still English literals in src/ — they reach a screen through ActionState, and they need catalog keys before a second locale ships
The fixed rate-limit window allows a brief 2x burst across a boundary; a sliding window needs a history table and is not worth it at these limits

title: Phase 2a: the block system and the public surface
delivered: src/modules/cms — the first feature module, so the first real test of the §11 contract rather than core describing itself
Module contract proven: requires + topo-sort puts core first however the list is written, and events.listens subscribes cms to core's settings.setupCompleted without either module importing the other
Typed block registry: every node Zod-validated against its own block before it is written, so jsonb stays a typed tree rather than a bag (§2 principle 12 names block content as its permitted case)
Unknown block types are refused, not dropped — dropping means the next save permanently deletes the sections a disabled plugin drew
Zod defaults applied on parse, so adding an optional prop to a block is not a data migration
v1 vocabulary: heading, text, button, columns, divider, spacer, faq, brand, nav — the blocks that need no module that does not exist yet
Blocks contribute their own JSON-LD: an FAQ block on a page is what puts FAQPage in the markup (§5)
One catch-all public route rendering block trees; a new page is an INSERT, live on the next request, with no build step (§32)
Site chrome as Sections: app/(public)/layout.tsx fetches two rows and renders them, containing no hardcoded site structure — menus are rows, not JSX
proxy.ts forwards the request path so the chrome's nav can mark the current entry while staying a server component
ContentRevision on every save, written inside the same transaction before the update; restoring is itself revisioned, so a restore is undoable (§37)
cms.ensureDefaults seeds header, footer and home idempotently on setup completion, so day one looks designed (§32)
Drafts are unreachable by URL — 'unlisted' is not a permission model — and excluded from the sitemap source
MASTER.md §11 records how a module reaches the public surface: block types, sitemap sources and seed content, never page routes
truncateSpine now derives from every installed module's manifest rather than core's barrel, so a new module is cleaned up between tests by existing
openFollowUps: No editor yet — this is Phase 2a. Drag-to-reorder, slash insertion, autosave and version-restore UI are Phase 2b; today a page is edited through the services
No admin screens for pages or sections, so the only way to author content is a service call
Image, gallery, product, booking, tip and paywall blocks wait on the modules that back them
Per-entity layout overrides and A/B variants with traffic splits (§32) are deliberately deferred
The catch-all does not yet serve locale-prefixed paths; §4.9's URL strategy lands in proxy.ts with EntityTranslation
generateMetadata and the page render each resolve the page, so a request costs two lookups until a request-scoped cache lands
No sitemap.xml, robots.txt or llms.txt route yet — cms.publishedPaths exists as the source, but the SEO engine that consumes it is Phase 3
ContentRevision has no pruning; an actively edited page grows a row per save

title: Phase 2b: the block editor
delivered: Edit forms derived from each block's own Zod schema, so the editor knows about fields and never about headings or FAQs — which is what makes §24's 'a plugin's block appears in the palette with zero editor changes' true rather than aspirational
Field kinds derived: text, multiline, boolean, choice (enum and literal union), and list-of-objects with sub-fields
A shape the derivation cannot draw yields no control rather than a broken one, so an exotic plugin schema loses one input instead of taking the editor down
Per-field hints live on the block definition, not in the editor: a paragraph renders as a textarea, and machinery like a nav's aria-label key is hidden from the owner
Every block declares a starter, parsed against its own schema at palette time — so adding a block cannot produce a tree that fails to save
Reorder by buttons as well as drag: drag alone is unusable with a keyboard or screen reader, and §15.7 puts a11y in the gates
Debounced autosave through cms.updatePage, with an aria-live save status and a retry on refusal
Version history with one-click restore; the restore is itself revisioned, so it is never a one-way door (§37)
Pages admin: list, create, publish/unpublish, and an owner-only repair that re-creates the starting site
Chrome admin editing the header and footer with the chrome palette — the same editor, a different context, which is the point of deriving the palette per context
Whole-tree saves rather than patches, so the server validates exactly what will be stored and ContentRevision is a faithful record
Verified in a browser end to end: autosave wrote through, the public page changed with no build, and restore reverted it
openFollowUps: No slash-command insertion. §32 names it, but it implies a rich-text surface and the text block is a textarea — what shipped is a block picker, which is the honest equivalent for now
No live responsive preview (§32); the editor shows controls, not a rendering
No drag between nesting levels — a block can be reordered within its list but not dragged into or out of a columns block
Adding a list item seeds empty strings, so a required sub-field is briefly invalid and the save is refused until it is filled; the message says so but the timing is awkward
cms.ensureDefaults renders in the audit trail as 'Cm — ensure defaults' because the prettifier strips a trailing s from the module name
Autosave has no conflict detection: two people editing one page will overwrite each other, last write wins
Testing the editor locally needs NODE_ENV=development even against a production build, because the session cookie is Secure and localhost is http

title: core/media, and the editor canvas with click-to-select
delivered: core/media: Asset table, upload, list, alt text, delete — the first consumer of the storage adapters, which had been sitting unused since they landed
Automatic responsive renditions (§36): AVIF and WebP at 400/800/1600/2400, never upscaled, with a format the local libvips cannot encode skipped rather than fatal
media.resolveImage returns srcset sources and intrinsic dimensions, so a page reserves space and never reflows when an image lands
Alt text lives on the asset rather than the block, so one description serves every use; the library flags images missing one, because §5 fails a page that renders without
SVG is stored but never resized and never served inline — it is a document that can carry script
Media served with immutable caching, since storage keys end in a random segment and a replacement produces a new key
The image block, and the first use of the resolve hook built in 2a: props name an asset, the URLs come from core/media at render time, so replacing a file updates every page showing it
An asset picker in the editor, derived like every other control — a new FieldHint control, not a special case in the editor
The editor canvas: a live preview beside the controls, rendered by the same renderBlocks the public page uses, with desktop and mobile widths (§32)
Click-to-select in both directions — clicking in the canvas selects the block card, selecting a card outlines it in the canvas
X-Frame-Options carved out for /preview only: DENY everywhere else, SAMEORIGIN plus frame-ancestors 'self' for the canvas
openFollowUps: The canvas shows the *saved* tree, so it follows autosave rather than keystrokes — a deliberate trade for the guarantee that the preview cannot disagree with the page
No inline editing and no visual drag yet: the canvas is a view, not an input surface
Editing a published page writes to the live site on autosave; there is no draft-then-publish workflow for changes to an already-published page
Uploads pass through the app rather than going straight to the bucket with a presigned URL, so a large file occupies the web process for its duration
blurhash is a column and nothing generates it (§4.5); a low-quality placeholder would also need a decision on which
Video and audio are stored but get no poster frame, duration or transcode
A page with several images costs one resolveImage query each — a request-scoped cache would collapse them

src/adapters/storage/local.ts reads process.env.NODE_ENV directly while the rest of the codebase reads through env(), so its production guard can disagree with the cookie logic about what production means
Deleting an asset does not check whether a block still points at it; the block renders nothing rather than breaking, but the owner gets no warning

title: Deleting media, and typing directly on the canvas
delivered: media.delete finally reachable: owner-only, hidden from staff rather than offered and refused, closing a service the admin could not call
Two-step confirmation, because deleting media is one of the few things here that genuinely cannot be undone — §37's reversible-in-one-action is unachievable once bytes leave the bucket

media.usage walks block trees with a jsonpath $.** so an image nested inside a columns block is found as readily as a top-level one; the id travels as a jsonpath variable rather than being concatenated in
Usage is a warning, not a refusal: an owner may well want the file gone, and a page pointing at a deleted asset renders a gap rather than an error — asserted by a test
Inline editing on the canvas: heading text, body copy and button labels are contenteditable in the preview and typed straight into
The mechanism belongs to the block — only a block knows which element shows which prop — while the decision to allow it belongs to the editor, which passes ctx.editable only when rendering a preview
Editor attributes appear in the preview and nowhere else, so the markup a visitor and a crawler receive is untouched

The canvas reports; the editor decides. Typed text becomes a postMessage the editor applies to the tree — the canvas never writes to the tree, which keeps the tree the source of truth and the rendering a view of it
The frame is deliberately not reloaded after an inline edit: it already shows what was typed, and refreshing mid-sentence would throw the caret away
Enter blurs rather than inserting a line break in a heading, and the text block renders as one editable region while typing because a caret cannot cross sibling paragraphs sensibly
openFollowUps: Only plain-string props are editable. Rich text (bold, inline links) is a spec decision before it is work: §32 forbids markup blobs, so it needs a constrained inline-node schema rather than stored HTML
No visual drag yet — the last of the four steps toward WYSIWYG, and the largest
An inline edit marks the tree dirty but does not reload the canvas, so a change that alters *layout* rather than text (not currently possible inline) would not be reflected until the next save
Deleting an asset still leaves any block pointing at it in place, holding a dead id; the block renders nothing, and nothing prunes the reference
media.usage runs one query per asset on the library screen — fine at this size, wants a single grouped query before a library gets large

title: Visual drag on the canvas — the last step to a visual editor
delivered: moveBlock: a pure, tested tree operation deciding whether a move is legal and what the tree becomes — kept out of the component because tree surgery is obviously correct until somebody drops a container into its own child

Refusals that matter: a container into its own subtree would detach that branch and lose it; a no-op; an unknown id; an 'inside' onto a block that holds nothing. Nine tests, including one asserting no move ever loses or duplicates a node
A drag grip rather than a draggable block: a draggable element swallows text selection, and these blocks are typed into
The grip is injected by the canvas script, not emitted by the renderer, so block components stay free of editor furniture
Drop indicators computed from rendered geometry — a line above or below by pointer midpoint, an outline for an empty container
Dragging beside a container's children moves a block in or out of it, so cross-container movement falls out of before/after rather than needing its own case

The DOM moves on drop for feedback, but that is a preview of the reported intent: the editor applies the move to the tree, and an illegal move leaves the tree untouched and snaps back on the next render
Verified end to end in a browser with real DragEvents: indicator computed 'before', canvas reordered, tree reordered, autosave kept a revision
openFollowUps: CDP mouse events cannot initiate HTML5 drag, so the browser check dispatches real DragEvents rather than moving a physical pointer — the listeners are exercised exactly as a user's drag would, but native drag *initiation* is not
No keyboard equivalent for moving a block between containers; the up/down buttons only reorder within a level, so nesting is mouse-only and that is an a11y gap §15.7 will want closed
No auto-scroll while dragging near the edge of the canvas
Rich text remains a spec decision: §32 forbids markup blobs, so inline formatting needs a constrained inline-node schema rather than stored HTML

title: core/seo — the layer that makes the site findable
delivered: Absolute canonical, Open Graph and Twitter card on every public page, built from the same row as the content — the SEO contract holds by construction rather than by an owner remembering a field

JSON-LD decided by what a page is, not by a setting: WebSite + Organization on the home page, BreadcrumbList everywhere else, and the owner schema.org type from setup used verbatim so a Photographer and a HairSalon emit genuinely different data

A sitemap index over per-locale sitemaps, assembled by calling the services modules named in seo.sitemapSources — the engine never learns what a page, product or gallery is, and a module ships its sitemap entry by existing
A sitemap source that throws is skipped with a warning: a broken module costs its own pages, not every other module’s
robots.txt blocking /admin, /login, /portal, /api and /preview — preview renders unpublished drafts, so a crawler following a leaked link must not index a page nobody published
llms.txt generated from the business profile and the same sitemap sources, listing only what is actually published
Redirects on slug change, written by cms.updatePage through ctx.callAsSystem in the same transaction as the rename — the page and the record of where it went commit together or not at all
Redirect resolution follows a chain of renames, gives up rather than looping, and retargets a row when a slug is taken back so a live page always beats a redirect

APP_URL is the only source of the canonical origin; a request that disagrees with it produces a warning, never the answer — a canonical built from the Host header is how a site tells a crawler its home is on somebody else’s domain
openFollowUps: Next matches a dynamic segment but never a dynamic part of one: app/sitemap-[locale].xml built cleanly and 404’d at runtime. The published URL is now a proxy rewrite onto /sitemaps/[locale], and a test asserts the address rather than the route — the build could not have caught this

Permanent redirects go out as 308, not the 301 §5 names: a server component cannot choose its status code. Permanent-versus-temporary is intact and search engines treat 308 as 301’s equal; the redirect row still records 301/302, so serving a literal 301 is a change in one place
hreflang is not emitted — §4.9 locale routing has not landed, so there is no second URL to point at
No generated OG images and no IndexNow ping on publish; both are named in §5 and neither blocks being indexed
The §15.2 SEO gate still needs the seeded demo site to crawl

title: Standing debts, first batch
delivered: contacts.merge refuses when both contacts have their own login. contacts.user_id is unique and 1:1, so a merge can keep only one: choosing silently either leaves a credential that still signs in and resolves to nobody, or destroys a real person’s password and sessions on one click. Verified by disabling the guard and watching the merge orphan a users row

The activity feed reads each service’s own summary instead of deriving prose from its name. The derivation stripped a trailing s from the module, so cms.ensureDefaults read as “Cm — ensure defaults”; the fallback stays for audit rows that outlive the service that wrote them, and no longer singularizes anything

The local storage adapter reads NODE_ENV and FREEHOLDER_UNSAFE_LOCAL_STORAGE through env() like everything else, and both are declared in the schema — a guard that decides for itself what production means can disagree with the platform that configured it

Request-scoped readers (core/settings/read.ts, modules/cms/read.ts) wrap the services in React cache(), so one render pass fetches the business profile and the page once rather than once per component that needs them
openFollowUps: Measured: a public page request made 4 getBusiness queries before and 2 after. It is not 1 because Next resolves generateMetadata in a separate cache scope from the render — halving it is what this seam can do
The remaining admin screens each call getBusiness once, so they gain nothing from the cache beyond consistency; the layout and page pair is where the duplicate was

PROJECT_BACKLOG claimed TimelineEventInput.subjectId was typed string against a uuid column. It is not: both timeline_events.subject_id and audit_log.subject_id are text, deliberately, because the column is polymorphic across entity types. No change, entry retired
Merging still has no confirmation step and cannot be undone (tracked separately)

title: The two gates that make unattended updates safe, plus signed images
delivered: Upgrade gate: CI pulls the previously published image, boots it against an empty database so it migrates to the released schema, writes a contact through it, applies this build, asserts the data survived and the site serves, then boots the old image again with FREEHOLDER_SKIP_MIGRATE=1 and asserts it still reads the new schema. That last step is the one that would otherwise be discovered by an owner at 3am
Data is seeded with SQL rather than through the UI on purpose: the claim under test is that migrations preserve data, and driving forms would make a failure ambiguous between the two

Schema-compatibility gate: refuses DROP TABLE/COLUMN, RENAME, retype, and a NOT NULL a previous release cannot satisfy, unless the migration carries the marker comment freeholder:schema-breaking with a reason. Matched per statement, so a later ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT cannot vouch for an earlier one that has none

The gate is quiet about everything expand-then-contract asks for — new tables, nullable columns, defaults, indexes, DROP NOT NULL — because a gate that fires on the recommended shape gets bypassed within a month

Images are signed keyless by digest (cosign, GitHub OIDC — no long-lived key to leak), with build provenance and an SPDX SBOM pushed to the registry. Verification commands are in the droplet verify checklist

Proved both directions: unit tests for the detector including the additive cases it must ignore, and the CLI run against a committed DROP COLUMN, which exited 1 with the expand-then-contract explanation
openFollowUps: The upgrade gate skips with a warning when no previously published image can be pulled — true on a fresh repository, and true for a pull request from a fork, whose token cannot read packages. A skipped gate is announced rather than silent, but it is still a skip
A migration acknowledged as schema-breaking is not yet reflected anywhere machine-readable: §39.3 wants schema_breaking on the release entry, and releases.json does not exist yet

The gate proves N-1 in one direction only — the old image reading the new schema. It does not prove the old *code* behaves correctly against it, which needs the old release’s own test suite and is not obviously worth the machinery

Migrations 0000-0005 predate the discipline and 0001 retypes a column. They cannot be edited — their hashes are in the journal of every database that has run them — so the baseline is recorded in the test rather than pretended away
arm64 images are still not built; signing does not change that

title: seed/ — Aurora Coast Photography
delivered: A six-page demo site — home, services, two service children, about, contact — with chrome, FAQ blocks, buttons and three generated photographs. Two levels deep on purpose, so breadcrumbs and the RIBA rule have something real to be right about

Installed by a service (demo.install) rather than a script, so it goes through the same permission check, transaction and audit row as an owner doing it by hand. Everything it writes goes through ordinary services, which means the demo can only contain content an owner could have produced themselves
A module that owns no tables and mounts no routes, whose requires: [cms] makes the topo-sort do real work — the block registry must be populated before a block tree can be validated against it
FREEHOLDER_SEED_DEMO=1 installs at boot if the site is empty. An env var rather than a route, because a route that installs a demo business is a route somebody eventually hits on a real instance
Refuses on an instance that already has pages, before writing anything, and there is deliberately no force flag: a flag that does not exist cannot be set by accident from a deploy recipe

Images are generated from SVG at install time and pushed through media.upload, so renditions, AVIF/WebP sources and intrinsic dimensions are all exercised without committing anyone's photographs, or megabytes, to the repository

The content is asserted against the checkable half of §5 in unit tests — one H1 per page, unique titles and descriptions within the lengths search results truncate at, alt text that describes rather than names a file, every page within three hops, no button pointing at a page that does not exist. A failure names the page rather than a URL

Verified end to end against a scratch database: booted with the flag, six pages published, sitemap listing all six, FAQPage and BreadcrumbList JSON-LD on a service child, and img tags carrying the real alt text with AVIF and WebP sources
openFollowUps: The seed installs cms content only. §11 wants each module to contribute its own seed data through its manifest; that becomes a registry when commerce and booking exist, and this is one file until then
No one-click purge from admin, which seed/README has promised since July
The §15.2 crawl gate is the next PR — this is the site it needed, and the unit assertions here are the subset that does not require a crawler

installDemo calls ensureDefaults and then updates the home page it creates, because updateSection updates and does not upsert. It mirrors what an owner does, but a create-or-update section service would be more honest
Copy is en only; EntityTranslation and locale routing have not landed, so a second locale has nothing to seed into

title: The SEO crawl gate and the a11y smoke test
delivered: A crawler that walks the seeded demo site from the root, following only links a search engine would follow, recording the shortest depth to each page — run against a real server rendering real pages, because the interesting failures live in the gap between the source and what a browser is sent

Per page: title, meta description, an absolute canonical that points at itself, exactly one H1, alt on every image, and JSON-LD that parses with a schema.org context and the properties that make each type useful rather than merely valid

Across the set: duplicate titles, duplicate descriptions, anything more than three clicks from home, pages in the sitemap that nothing links to, and pages linked from the site that the sitemap never mentions
hreflang is checked only when the instance publishes more than one locale — demanding it of a single-locale site would train people to add tags describing a translation that does not exist
An accessibility smoke test running axe-core inside a jsdom window over the four public templates, restricted to rules that mean something without layout

Both gates run in CI against the built image with FREEHOLDER_SEED_DEMO=1, and the runner refuses to proceed unless the demo actually installed — a crawl gate over an empty instance is a green tick that checked one page
Proved failing on a real page rather than a fixture: added a second H1 and blanked an asset's alt text in a live database, and the gate exited 1 naming both pages and the image
openFollowUps: page-has-heading-one comes back *incomplete* under jsdom because axe needs layout, so it is out of the rule list — found while testing, and the reason the gate now reports undecided rules instead of counting them as passes. landmark-one-main lands in the same state on the real pages

No browser, so focus order, focus visibility, keyboard traps and reflow at 320px are all unchecked. Colour contrast is covered separately by tests/core/tokens.test.ts, which enforces WCAG AA on token pairings in both schemes
The crawl follows links only; a page reachable solely by a form submission or a redirect is invisible to it

JSON-LD validation is against a hand-listed set of the types we emit, not the schema.org vocabulary. It catches a BreadcrumbList without positions; it would not catch a misspelled property on a type nobody here uses
The a11y smoke strips the page's scripts before parsing, so anything rendered only after hydration is not audited. Nothing on the public surface currently is

title: The forms module — the first module whose public surface writes
delivered: Forms as definitions: fields are rows in jsonb and the validator that accepts a visitor's answers is derived from them, so the two cannot disagree. Seven field kinds, each mapping to an input a browser renders natively with the right keyboard on a phone

An anonymous submission reaches the spine through contacts.resolve and ctx.callAsSystem — never contacts.create — so a stranger can cause a Contact to exist and nothing else. Verified in a browser: a real submission produced one contact, lowercased, sourced form:contact, with contact.created and form.submitted on the timeline

The first module to contribute a *block type*. A new `blocks` entry on the module manifest registers it at boot in dependency order, which is the seam §24 promises plugins: the block joins the palette, the editor derives its controls from the block's Zod schema, and the editor changes not at all

Two traps that cost a visitor nothing: a honeypot hidden from layout and from assistive technology, and a time trap whose timestamp is HMAC-signed — an unsigned one is worthless, since a bot that reads the field can post any value it likes

Neither trap rejects. §36 wants a quarantine queue rather than a bin: suspected spam is stored, flagged with the reason in words, kept out of the CRM, and rescuable in one click — and rescuing it resolves the contact then, exactly as an unflagged submission would have. Verified in a browser: a bot filling the honeypot got the same thank-you, was stored as spam, and created no contact

No client component on the public surface. The submission result travels back in the URL and is rendered server-side, because §5 and the SEO gate both rest on the public HTML having no hydration boundary. BlockRenderContext gained `query` for it
Only a code travels in that URL, never a message: a page that echoes arbitrary text from its own query string is a phishing page waiting for a crafted link

The merge-completeness gate was widened from core's barrel to every module's tables — forms is the first module with a contact_id column, and the gate could not have seen it. Modules declare their own repoint with registerContactReference(). Proved by disabling the registration and watching the gate name the table
Admin: a forms list with the quarantine count surfaced, and a per-form submissions view with received/flagged/all and a one-click rescue
The demo site now ships a real enquiry form on /contact, so the a11y smoke checks real labels against real controls and the SEO crawler walks a page that writes
openFollowUps: No form builder UI: forms are created through the service, and the admin lists them but cannot yet add or edit one. An owner without API access has the demo form and nothing else

The rate limit is per form rather than per visitor. An anonymous surface has no trustworthy identity, and Next does not hand a Server Action a client address honestly — so a determined single attacker can exhaust one form's window for everybody. Wants the same trusted-IP work as registerOwner
`notify` is stored and nothing sends it: there is no mail adapter yet, so an owner learns about a submission by opening the admin

Server-side validation messages are not shown to a no-JS visitor — only a generic failure. Browsers enforce required and type=email natively, so the specific message is a backstop, but a JS-less visitor who defeats native validation gets less help than they should
No spam signal beyond the two traps: no Turnstile, no reputation, no content heuristics. §36 names Turnstile as optional and it is not wired
Submissions are never pruned, and a busy form's quarantine grows without limit

React emits `autoComplete` in camelCase in the server-rendered HTML. Checked with a real HTML parser rather than assumed: attribute names are case-insensitive, so a browser reads autocomplete=email and autofill works. Cosmetic, noted so nobody re-investigates

title: First-party analytics, and the first half of the funnel
delivered: Page views recorded server-side during the render, from identifiers the proxy mints. Nothing to block, no client bundle, no third-party host, and it works with JavaScript off — so the traffic chart describes the traffic rather than the subset that ran a tag

identify() backfills a visitor's whole history onto the contact they turn out to be, not just what happens next. Without it a contact's first recorded moment is the form they submitted rather than the three pages they read first, and 'which page brings me enquiries' is unanswerable

Analytics listens for forms.submitted on the bus and never imports forms; forms does not know analytics exists. An instance with forms switched off records no conversions and breaks nothing. Verified in the request graph: boot reports 5 modules, 60 services, 2 listeners

What is not stored is asserted by a test over the whole row shape: no IP, no user-agent, no fingerprint, no third-party identifier. §36 puts third-party pixels on the anti-roadmap and a first-party rebuild of the same surveillance would be worse
Referrers are reduced to the host — google.com answers the owner's question, and the full referring URL is a fragment of a stranger's browsing history
The proxy refuses to mint an identifier at all for /admin, /login, /preview, /portal, /api and assets. The cheapest way to be sure a number is honest is never to record it

Crawlers and prefetches are filtered before recording. Verified against a live instance: four pages browsed as a person were recorded with referrer google.com; the same request as Googlebot, and a request to /admin, recorded nothing
Merging two contacts brings the visitor history with it — registered through the module seam added with forms
An admin traffic screen: five counts, a per-day bar list built from rows rather than a canvas (readable by a screen reader, prints, no client JS), top pages and top referrers
openFollowUps: One insert per page view, inside the request. Fine against a local Postgres at this scale; an obvious batching candidate once core/jobs exists, and written down rather than assumed

No consent gate. §30 models ConsentRecord with an analytics purpose and nothing reads it yet — an EU-facing instance needs that wired before the cookie is defensible there. The identifier is first-party and cross-site tracking is impossible by construction, which is the argument, not a ruling
No retention limit and no pruning: the table grows forever. Wants a setting and a job
The funnel stops at 'became a contact' because the money tables do not exist yet. §4.7's full visit → lead → quote → paid is one join away and cannot be written until quotes and invoices are real
Core Web Vitals are named in §36 as first-party-tracked and are not collected; that needs a client-side reporter, which is the first thing here that would

The bus listener reads the visitor cookie from the request. When the transactional outbox lands (§39 roadmap) a replayed event will have no request, and the code already degrades to recording the conversion without the visitor link — but the link is the valuable half
Sessions roll over after 30 minutes of quiet, which is convention rather than measurement

title: Serious bot detection, and an owner toggle for it
delivered: Replaced one hand-written regex with isbot (maintained, public domain) plus a signal-based classifier over request shape. A hand-written list is wrong in both directions from the day it is written, and the interesting bots are the ones that do not declare themselves

Signals beyond the user-agent: a missing or */* Accept, no Accept-Language, and none of the Sec-Fetch-* headers every browser since 2019 sends on a navigation. Two independent signals is a program; one is somebody's unusual browser, so one is 'suspected' rather than 'bot'
Three outcomes rather than two, because the honest answer to a plausible user-agent with no browser headers is 'probably not a person, but not worth deleting a visit over'

Reversed the earlier decision to drop bot requests at write time. Everything is recorded with a verdict and its reasons, and filtered at read time — the same choice the spam quarantine makes. A call made once, invisibly, that can never be seen or undone is the wrong shape for a judgement that is sometimes wrong

An owner toggle, stored as the analytics module's own configuration and validated against the settingsSchema its manifest declares — §11's settingsSchema used for the first time, with new core services settings.setModuleConfig and settings.getModuleConfig
Defaults parsed on read as well as write, so a module that adds a setting later gets its default on instances configured before it existed
The excluded count is reported whichever way the toggle is set: an owner deciding whether to trust the other five numbers needs to know how much was left out

Verified against a live instance with five differently-shaped requests: a real browser recorded human; Googlebot and GPTBot recorded bot; a scraper sending a copied Chrome user-agent and nothing else recorded bot with three reasons; an old Safari — a real person — recorded suspected with one
openFollowUps: No reverse-DNS verification of declared crawlers, which is the correct way to know a self-declared Googlebot is one. It is a DNS round trip per request and belongs behind a cache and a job

No IP reputation or datacentre ranges — the strongest signal available, and deliberately absent: §4.7 stores no IP, and adding one to catch bots would build the surveillance §36 rules out in order to measure traffic
No behavioural signals yet: a visitor reading forty pages in twenty seconds is obvious and currently invisible, because computing it at write time costs a query per view
Recording bots rather than dropping them means a heavily crawled site accumulates rows faster. Compounds the existing lack of retention and pruning
The toggle is instance-wide rather than per-report. That is the right default; a per-report override is a small addition if anyone wants it
